newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - LanChile delays U.S. alliance.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - LanChile delays U.S. alliance.

text.p: Although aviation sources had expected LanChile to announce a strategic alliance with a U.S. airline this fall, a top executive told Reuters this week the pact would not be struck for another year.

"In the medium term -- one year -- we have to have an alliance. We feel the world is moving to there," said Ignacio Cueto, president of Lan Cargo Group, in an interview Tuesday. He said an announcement was likely before year-end 1997.

The Cueto family and two other partners control LanChile and all-cargo FastAir, both based in Santiago. The airlines field 39 aircraft. Combined they carry the eighth most cargo through Miami International Airport, according to statistics compiled by the Dade County Aviation Department.

Cueto said Lan is "thinking and talking with" several airlines, including AMR Corp's American Airlines and UAL Corp's United Airlines. Cueto and his partners are also on the prowl for arrangements with Latin American airlines. These could include alliances, investments or outright purchase, depending on the circumstance, Cueto said.
"We are studying many companies," he said. "We are open to different companies in our zone." He mentioned especially Argentina or Peru.
Besides agreements with other Latin American airlines, LanChile and Fast hope to win more routes and grow and consolidate within Latin America. They would like to connect their network with Asia.

Cueto also hopes to strike some agreements with Asian carriers for cargo. He sees strong growth in trade between Latin America and Asia. "We think it is going to continue to be a very big market," he said.
"We want to be there and we want to prepare to be number one in that (Latin America-Asia) market," Cueto said.
"We are not planning to fly to Asia," he said.

Although Cueto has no plans to move his hub from Miami International Airport, because of the location close to both Asia and South America, "We think LAX (Los Angeles International Airport) is a very good gateway."
The Cueto group also have a 24.9 percent interest in Miami-based Florida West International Airlines, which is in the process of getting certification from the Federal Aviation Administration.
